note: Grounding for dart-flutter-reviewer. Two kinds, deliberately not conflated. 'vendored' files are upstream text reproduced byte-for-byte: their hash must equal upstream's, and a mismatch means drift. 'derived' files are rules written for this harness that cite first-party sources: their hash pins OUR text, and the sources are pinned by version or checked-on date. Upstream moving does not make a derived rule wrong — it makes it unverified. Hashing live documentation HTML was considered and rejected: it changes for navigation and analytics edits, and an alarm that fires for non-reasons gets switched off.

policy.onVendoredDrift: re-vendor from upstream and re-pin in the same change; until then the reviewer says the file is unverified and stops relying on it
policy.onDerivedSourceDrift: open an issue, re-derive the affected rules, bump computedHash in the same change
